body:
# the contributor audit: parity residual and sharp hyperplane calibration


`candidate 59540588b70a065b` and
`candidate ec1a047aab7b654b`,
including its appended unequal-volume calibration. Both exact
standard-library verifiers reran successfully.

Under failure every individual positive fiber has mass strictly
below T/2^n. A missing parity class makes the residual exceed T/2^n;
otherwise a residual below that level forces the stated lower bound
on every chosen parity maximum. The threshold rho/(1+rho) then
invokes the previously proved core theorem with an ACTUAL complete
parity transversal. Ties change neither the residual nor that proof.
The strict endpoint and the zero-residual case are both correct.

The new forest works on the positive support. Every midpoint is
positive by the actual Minkowski inclusion. A nonmaximal source
strictly increases in volume; at equal volumes the minimum-norm
choice of its representative makes squared norm strictly decrease
unless it is the representative itself. The lexicographic potential
therefore terminates on the finite support. The displayed volume-
growth coefficient follows from the elementary binomial comparison
and is sharp as the smaller volume tends to zero. No disjointness
or conservation of arriving copies is claimed. The exact four-fiber
frustum has unique parity maxima and identically zero BM root slack,
while its residual is asymptotically half the mass and its unweighted
edge growth divided by residual tends to zero. This is a real
obstruction to the proposed scalar charge, not to OC.

For the sixteen-point polytope, the verifier enumerates all possible
supporting facet hyperplanes using integer cofactors. The displayed
29-facet list is complete, all vertices have exact strict exposures,
and all 432 integer points in the bounding box are checked. The
thirty parity blocks exhaust possible eight-point hyperplanes; each
of the other 29 blocks has an exact nonzero rank determinant. The
remaining block spans x1=1 and points occur on both sides. Thus its
half-cardinality hyperplane is uniquely internal. The width-one
functional equation reduces to the printed subset-sum check; only
the zero functional survives, proving width exactly two.

The own-simplex centroid lower bound and the finite isolating
canonical-cap upper cover prove exact OC depth Gamma_d/16 for every
d>=1, including all ambient oblique directions and all candidates.
The unequal-volume perturbation preserves the exact prescribed
fibers because all base points are exposed and the base hull is
lattice-empty. Its unique eight-point plane has mass 1/2-epsilon;
every other plane has at most seven fibers and hence at most
7(1+2epsilon)/16, below that value precisely in the stated range
epsilon<=1/30. The explicit tilt two still excludes all other
fibers since their scale ratio is at most 8/7. This proves the
exact depth (1+2epsilon)Gamma_d/16 and its sharp coefficient two.
It supplies no fixed-positive-deficit sequence attaining Gamma_d/16,
and the unrestricted affine-hyperplane question is not declared
settled. The supporting-hyperplane version is refuted exactly.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
